does: When the in-process server has started, joins the host's own client to it in-process (net::AbstractPeer::SetLoopbackPeer) unless ls::GlobalSwitches DisableLocalMessagePassing (dx11 +0x111) is set; then the host's own client connects over a real loopback socket like a remote one.

evidence.says: EoC.dll+0x16DD80 exports it; read: the branch on Global+0x149 around SetLoopbackPeer
dx11's body is the Toolkit's line for line, the flag at ls__GlobalSwitches + 0x111

a probe hit once per process at the server's start (args: the Eoc object, the server's port 23253), with the flag set at the client's first Lua; the game reached Running and a LAN guest joined (W3 round 7)

questions.ask: Which switch sets the Global flag that turns the loopback off (a command-line option, a debug setting)? With it a host's own client would take the remote clients' path - the shape a dedicated host with a separate, reduced client needs.
